Shipping container types

A standard dry container measures 20 or 40 feet and carries general cargo. A high-cube variant adds roughly a foot of internal height, which matters for light, bulky goods. Reefers hold a temperature range and need a power point at the terminal, so booking one usually means extra paperwork. Open-top boxes suit cargo loaded by crane from above.

Choosing between them

Match the box to the cargo rather than to the rate: overpaying for a reefer on dry goods wastes money, and under-specifying humidity control ruins paper products. The terminal charges dwell fees after the free window, so plan the pickup before the vessel berths.
